sentences.text: Wargosuchus was an extinct genus of baurusuchid crocodyliforms that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous. This animal possessed a robust skull, distinguishing it from many of its contemporaries.

The fossil record consists of MOZ-PV 6134, which includes a partial right premaxilla, maxilla, and skull roof. Researchers identified the genus by specific skull features including a midline groove on the frontal bones, a large depression for olfactory bulbs, and an enlarged premaxillary tooth followed by a deep pit for the lower jaw tooth.

The genus was described by Agustín Martinelli and Diego Pais in 2008 based on a fragmentary skull found near Neuquén in the Santonian-age Bajo de la Carpa Formation. The only known species is the type species Wargosuchus australis.
Wargosuchus lived alongside four other mesoeucrocodylian taxa: the common Notosuchus and the rare Cynodontosuchus, Lomasuchus, and Gasparinisuchus.
Wargosuchus is classified as a reptile and belongs to the family Baurusuchidae. It also belongs to the parent group Pissarrachampsinae.
Wargosuchus lived during the Santonian stage, approximately 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
